$comment: DOCS-AUDIT-3. Binds every published number that traces to a benchmark run to the artifact it
came from, so a future measurement change makes the published page FAIL a check instead of
silently diverging from it. This is the machine-readable half of docs/published-claims-inventory.md
(DOCS-AUDIT-1); that file stays the human narrative, this one is what CI can run.
Deliberately a CHECKER, not a generator: both published artifacts are hand-authored HTML with no
build step (see the two-artifacts rule), and regenerating them would replace prose written by a
person with template output. Making divergence loud achieves the chunk's goal without that.
Claims with NO artifact - external/competitor figures cited from papers, and narrative about
past runs - are listed in `untraceable` so their absence here is a recorded decision rather
than an oversight.
metric: a key of a systems[] entry in the run's longmemeval_s_terransoul.json.
scale/decimals: how the artifact value is rendered before matching (0.9504 -> 95.0 at 1dp).
needle: the EXACT published substring, with {value} where the number appears.

artifacts.$comment-arms: head-full500-* is the canonical set: one embedder (embeddinggemma) AND one code version (HEAD, 2026-07-27), one arm per process. The max100-full500-* arms are 2026-07-25 code, and max100-full500/ additionally ran the harness-default embedder — both kept on disk as evidence, neither safe to compare across.
artifacts.$comment-arms-2: CORRECTED 2026-07-27: full500-think and full500-research still pointed at the max100-* (2026-07-25 code) arms while the comment above declared head-full500-* canonical — so the manifest contradicted itself, and any claim bound to `think` would have been checked against a different code version from every other arm. Both now point at head-full500-*, and all four are embeddinggemma. The repoint MOVES the think numbers a long way (NDCG@10 93.78 on 2026-07-25 code, 87.25 at HEAD) — that delta is a real regression under investigation, not a manifest artifact, which is precisely why it must be the checked value.

$comment: MAX-100-26. docs/bench-100-percent-semantics.md records, per bench, whether 100 is emittable AT ALL.
Until this block existed that file was prose, and prose does not stop anyone publishing a 100 % target
next to a bench whose judge cannot produce one - which is how a cross-bench '100 % in thinking MAX'
goal got set over benches with incompatible ceilings. The checker now parses the table and fails any
perfect-score claim it can attribute to a row marked capped.
aliases: page prose spells benches more loosely than the table's first column. An alias declared for a
bench with no row in the table is REPORTED, so deleting a row cannot silently disarm the guard.
exempt: an escape hatch that costs a written reason, and the quote must SPAN the number it exempts
(quoting text that merely sits nearby would silence every other claim on the page). Prefer wording the
sentence so it states the cap - the checker already reads 'not emittable', 'cannot emit', 'is not
reached' and friends as honouring the table rather than breaking it.

requireSameEmbedder.$comment: Every artifact compared against another in the same claim must share an embedder. The chat arm was run without LONGMEM_EMBED_MODEL and silently used the harness default (mxbai-embed-large) while the others used embeddinggemma, which invalidated a cross-arm comparison for a full day before anyone read the report headers. This turns that into a failure.

$comment-floors: The four `me-*-rrf` / `index-rrf-*` entries below are the 95.1 / 95.9 FLOOR family. They are EXPECTED to
report MISMATCH against the current artifacts (95.04 / 95.76) and that is the point: under
rules/bench-never-regress.md a published number is regained, not lowered, so the mismatch is the open
obligation made loud. Do NOT silence them by editing the page down. They go green when a run clears the
floor - or, if the old record is ever forensically proven to be a measurement error, when the owner signs
off on retiring it. The 2026-07-27 audit annotated every one of these on-page with the measured value, its
artifact, and its date, so a reader sees the floor and the measurement together.
claims.note: Fig 12, panel 10 (Hybrid Fusion). Renamed 2026-07-27 from `me-fig8-cov-ndcg`, which sent a reader to a figure that does not carry this number.
Fig 16, left column. Renamed 2026-07-27 from `me-fig17-ships-rrf` - it is Fig 16, not Fig 17.

Fig 14 card 1 and the Stage-12 table. The needle read `NDCG@10 ≥ {value}` until 2026-07-27: the `>=` asserted the floor was CURRENTLY being met, which is a strictly stronger claim than citing the floor and is false while the measurement sits below it. The operator was removed from the page (not the number), so the needle drops it too.

Claim 3 of the inventory, REBOUND 2026-07-27. The old needle quoted the sentence calling chat 'byte-identical to the validated retrieval path (LongMemEval-S NDCG@10 95.1)'. That sentence was deleted rather than re-numbered: chat measures 93.78 against rrf's 95.04 and 140 of 500 orderings differ, so the identity assertion was false in kind, not off by digits - a never-regress question does not arise for a claim that was never a measurement of chat. Fig 17 now publishes chat's own measured value and this needle binds it.

Fig 17's measured-state footer, added 2026-07-27. The figure used to draw four increasing rungs; it now prints the measured order underneath, and these three claims pin every number in it so the shape cannot silently drift back.
think is BELOW chat here. That is a real regression on current code - the same arm on 2026-07-25 code matched chat to four decimals - and it is published as such rather than omitted.

untraceable.why: Competitor/baseline numbers quoted from cited papers or vendor self-reports. They must trace to a source citation, not to a run of ours; checking them against our artifacts would be a category error. NOTE 2026-07-27: this entry used to list 'R@10 57.2, R@100 76.9/43.7, NDCG@10 45.0/49.9' as competitor figures. They were not competitor figures - they were OURS, from a 2026-06-09 LoCoMo run, spliced against a 2026-06-27 rrf_emb run to manufacture a dense-channel lift that the matched data reverses. Section 5.2 now carries the corrected within-run pair and the forensic note; misfiling our own stale numbers as somebody else's is how they escaped checking for a month.

This entry previously read 'External survey figure, not ours' and was therefore deliberately unbound - wrongly. 68.3 % IS ours: MTEB LoCoMo R@10 for `rrf_rerank`, BENCH-LCM-8, 2026-05-12 (benchmark/terransoul/locomo-mteb/README.md, benchmark/README.md).
